schema_note: Experiment B's LOOKUP gold: which SECTION answers a single-fact question. Frozen on authoring; never regenerate from system output.
method: HAND-AUTHORED, one primary answering section per query. The system's own predictions were never consulted: no query_log, no selected_sections, no retrieval run, no Phase-8 output.

Stratum S (standards) is ENRICHMENT-INDEPENDENT: each query is built from a cue in the frozen answer suite (eval/gold, via sec_gold_candidates) that occurs in EXACTLY ONE section of the corpus. Its provenance is the answer gold, not anything Phase 3 or Phase 4 produced.

Strata L and H are authored from quote-validated key values and breadcrumbs. Those values are verbatim spans of the document (parse_section_enrichment checks every quote against the section text), so the FACTS are the document's; what is enrichment-dependent is only which requirements were available to ask about. Stated as a limit below.

Stratum M is semantic mismatch, written by hand so that the query's distinguishing vocabulary does NOT appear in the answering section. Each record carries the measured term overlap, so the claim is checkable rather than asserted.

`14. Desktop/Console for LED Video Wall` and its EPEAT requirement are deliberately ABSENT. That omission is an aggregate-selection adjudication (docs/rag_v2/goal_scorecard.md, 2026-11-03) and making it a lookup benchmark example would be inventing a test from a known failure.
limits: ONE document, one corrigendum family. Nothing here generalises to another corpus.

A requirement Phase 4 never extracted cannot appear in strata L, H or M -- those are authored from the enrichment, so the gold is blind in the same places the enricher is. Stratum S exists to be unaffected by that, and is the subset to trust when the arms disagree.

`answer_sections` with more than one entry are MULTI-BEARER: the requirement genuinely appears in each. A hit on any one is correct, which makes those records easier than the single-bearer ones; they are marked so they can be reported apart.
There is no negative stratum (queries the document does not answer). Lookup abstention is a different measurement and is not part of Experiment B.

Records H-04 to H-07 ask WHICH SECTION covers a topic rather than for a specific value. That is a legitimate section-finding question and it is an easier one: there is no figure to get wrong. They are a seventh of the set and can be reported apart.

S-01 and M-05 are a deliberate PAIR: the same requirement (IEC 60297) asked once in the document's own words and once in avoided vocabulary. S-02/M-06 and S-09/M-07 pair the same way. Comparing an arm's result within a pair isolates phrasing from content.

records.query: Which processor is specified for the nodes of the SOC and security analytics cluster?
records.provenance: 5.3 HCI-1 Node/Server Hardware and Software; the subject 'SOC and security analytics' is in the PARENT heading 5. HCI-1, not in 5.3's own. THREE OTHER SECTIONS NAME THE SAME PROCESSOR as a cross-reference (8. NBAD Central Infrastructure, 12. DAM Central Infrastructure, 17.2 HCI-2 Node/Server). 5.3 is the section that SPECIFIES it for this cluster and the others restate it for theirs, so the single answer stands -- but an arm landing on a restating section is a near miss rather than a blunder, and `near_bearers` records that judgement instead of leaving it to be discovered later.
